champion: Metastatic Malignant Mesothelioma to the Tongue
ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic Malignant Mesothelioma to the Tongue

facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old nonsmoking man presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
multiple pleural thickenings and marked effusion on the left side
nodular growth appeared on the mid third of the tongue
Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1
Negative for methylthioadenosine phosphorylase
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
The disease remained stable until July 2023
